app.desc: Calculate your aura points in 7 questions and share your card. Gamer Mode, School Mode, and Party Mode.

app.fine2: It all happens on your phone.
app.shareText: I got {score} aura points. Calculate yours at farmearaura.com
about: farmearaura.com is an aura points calculator: seven everyday situations, three modes (Gamer, School, Party & Crush), and a final score that turns into a card you can share. No account needed, no photos uploaded, and nothing gets saved -- the whole thing runs right on your phone.
Besides the quiz, the site has aura duels: you can vote on who has more aura between everyday archetypes or between historical figures, and check out the ranking built from everyone's votes.

guide.title: What Is Aura Farming: Meaning, Origin, and Rules | farmearaura.com
guide.desc: Aura farming means racking up imaginary charisma points without trying. The meaning, where the term comes from, how much each situation is worth, and the rules of aura farming.
guide.answer: Aura farming means racking up imaginary charisma points by doing things that look effortless: staying calm, never explaining yourself, and never checking for a reaction. The points aren't real and nobody's actually counting, but the social rule behind them is.
origin: The phrase pairs two words from different worlds. Farming comes from gaming: repeating an action over and over to rack up resources, experience, or loot. Aura is used here as a stand-in for presence — whatever someone gives off the second they walk into a room. Aura farming, then, is stacking up presence on purpose.

The term had already been floating around gaming and anime communities, but it exploded in mid-2025 with one very specific video: an 11-year-old boy from Indonesia named Rayyan Arkan Dikha, wearing dark sunglasses and traditional dress, dancing on the bow of a canoe while his team rowed behind him.

The video wasn't a TikTok stunt. Dikha was doing a real job in the Pacu Jalur, a centuries-old traditional boat race held in Indonesia's Riau province. His role is called Togak Luan — the dancer who stands at the bow to hype up the rowers, a position usually held by kids because it demands serious balance. Dikha told the BBC the moves came to him spontaneously, and months later he was named a tourism ambassador for his province.

That contrast is what defined the term: someone doing something genuinely difficult while looking like it costs them nothing, without ever glancing at the camera. That's the practical definition of aura farming.
guide.pointsIntro: There's no official scale. The convention is to use round, exaggerated numbers, because the size of the number is part of the joke — nobody says "+12 aura," they say "+50,000." Points get handed out in comments, group chats, or among friends, always after the fact.
ledger: Catching a cup before it hits the floor and not breaking conversation
Answering a question correctly without having paid attention at all
Getting the top score and putting the paper away without a word
Waving at someone who was waving at the person behind you
Sending three follow-up texts explaining your first one
Deleting a message the other person already saw
guide.pointsOutro: When the total drops below zero, that's negative aura, and if it's really low, that's aura bankruptcy. It's a joke between friends — nobody's actually keeping score.
guide.rulesIntro: As silly as it sounds, the meme encodes some pretty recognizable social rules. These are the ones that show up in almost every video:
rules: Explaining a good move cancels it out. If you have to narrate it, it doesn't count.
Staying calm reads as control. Reacting instantly reads as nerves.
Checking to see if anyone noticed erases all the aura the action just earned.
This is the central rule of the whole meme.
The recovery matters more than not falling.
Tripping and walking it off without looking back earns more aura than never tripping at all.
Do something for someone with no audience.
Aura goes up when the move had no witnesses to begin with.
Say "that was aura" and you lose all your aura.
Naming it kills it. It's the one absolute rule.
guide.loseIntro: Negative aura is the fun half of the meme, and it almost always comes down to the same thing: needing someone else to confirm something for you. The most common cases:
lose: Repeating a joke nobody heard the first time.
Explaining why your joke was actually funny.
Texting "?" when someone leaves you on read.
Announcing how much something cost when nobody asked.
Asking someone to delete a photo (everyone goes and looks now).
Making up an excuse nobody asked for.
glossary: Deliberately racking up charisma through actions that look effortless.
A made-up unit for scoring a moment. Always round, always exaggerated.

Extreme negative aura. Used when someone stacks up several missteps in a row.
The internet's nickname for Rayyan Arkan Dikha, the boy from the canoe video.
Short clips that set an everyday moment — or an anime scene — to epic music. Characters who barely move, staying eerily calm, are the favorite format; Piccolo is one of the most-used.
faq: It means racking up imaginary charisma points by doing things that look effortless: staying calm, skipping the explanations, and never checking for a reaction. It combines farming, the gaming term for grinding out resources by repeating an action, with aura, used here as a stand-in for someone's presence.
Where does the term aura farming come from?

It exploded in mid-2025 after a video of Rayyan Arkan Dikha, an 11-year-old boy from Riau, Indonesia, dancing on the bow of a canoe during the Pacu Jalur boat race. His calm, effortless-looking performance became the template for the term.
What does aura mean on TikTok?

On TikTok, aura doesn't refer to the esoteric energy field — it means someone's charisma or social presence. It's used like a score: a person gains or loses aura depending on how good or bad they looked in a given moment.
How do you farm aura in real life?

Don't explain what you did, react late and stay calm, never fish for a reaction, win quietly, and recover well when something goes wrong. The main rule is that announcing you're farming aura cancels out all the aura you just earned.

A made-up unit for scoring how charismatic a moment was. There's no official scale — the convention is round, exaggerated numbers, like +1,000 for a good comeback or −50,000 for an embarrassing moment.
Yes. It's handed out as a joke when someone gets embarrassed or pushes too hard on something. When the total gets low enough, people call it aura bankruptcy. It's humor, not a judgment on the person.
Who is the boat kid from the aura farming video?

Rayyan Arkan Dikha, an 11-year-old boy from the Kuantan Singingi regency in Riau, Indonesia. His role in the Pacu Jalur boat race was Togak Luan — the dancer at the bow who hypes up the rowers. He told the BBC the moves came to him spontaneously, and he was later named a tourism ambassador for his province.
Does aura farming have anything to do with aura colors?

No. They're two different uses of the same word. The esoteric version of aura refers to a supposed energy field with colors and meanings. The TikTok version is a metaphor for charisma and works as a joke score, with no connection to spiritual beliefs.
What is the aura points calculator?
A free seven-question quiz that gives you a total aura score and generates a shareable card. It runs right in your browser, doesn't ask for an account or photos, and doesn't save any data.
